A `PartialDeep`/deep-partial type says that partial leaf is legal while the runtime silently discards siblings → type lies about behavior (fail-clear violation; real bug for JS consumers). Use a hand-rolled **2-level Partial**, NOT PartialDeep: `type ThemeOverride = { role?: Partial<TheoTheme['role']>; status?: Partial<TheoTheme['status']> }`. Each group optional, each leaf complete — this matches the merge exactly and needs no dep. Both are correct; the defaultTheme-in-context form is simpler and can't leak undefined. Do NOT throw on missing provider — the plan wants fail-safe fallback, not a boundary error.\n- **[INFO] — Gotcha 2: `jsx: \"react-jsx\"` means NO default `import React` needed in the `.tsx` test.** Only named imports for hooks used directly (`createContext`/`useContext` in `theme.tsx`; none needed in the test). The probe pattern: a tiny component calls `useTheoTheme()` and either (a) renders a string token into `<Text>` for `toContain` frame assertions, or (b) writes the value to an outer `let captured` for the EC-4 object compare. Render via `ink-testing-library`, then your accepted LOCAL one-tick await before reading. Watch: never render a `string | undefined` token (`text`) as a `<Text>` **child** (undefined child warns) — it's only valid as `color={token}`.\n- **[INFO] — Gotcha 4: `toEqual` is structural, so a freshly-spread `{}`-override object equals `defaultTheme`; the trap is elsewhere.** `toEqual` recurses (new nested objects are fine) and treats `text: undefined` as equal to absent, so an undefined-safe `text` token won't break it — no need for `toStrictEqual`. Real risks: (1) using `toBe` (identity) instead of `toEqual` — would fail on any new object; (2) the merge injecting a key absent from `defaultTheme` (only a risk if the type/merge drift from the 2-level shape in Gotcha 1). If EC-4 fails despite a new object, the cause is a broken merge returning the raw `{}` — which is exactly what the test should catch, so a failure here is signal, not a false negative.\n\n## Recommended action\n- Encode the override prop as the **2-level `ThemeOverride`** (`role?: Partial<...>; status?: Partial<...>`), not PartialDeep — and add `| undefined` to the prop only if a `theme={undefined}` call site exists (exactOptionalPropertyTypes rejects explicit `undefined` on a bare optional).
